nodes.label: Tenant feedback AI insights (summarize + chat) for super admins
Feedback corpus is fenced as untrusted DATA, never instructions
Hard corpus caps (300 rows / 800 chars / 90 days) are the only guard against context-length errors and surprise OpenAI bills
Super-admin gate enforced in application code because service_role bypasses RLS and is_super_admin()
Malformed ```json theme block degrades to an empty theme list rather than failing the summary
Browser-supplied chat history is truncated so a stuck admin-page loop cannot push a megabyte per keystroke
Backfill a missing Stripe payment_intent id onto a payments row
Lookups must run on the Stripe platform the payment was created on (payments.platform_account, default 'uk' legacy client)
Three-tier reconciliation: checkout session id, then amount+date window, then customer email — each retried on the platform account
Veriff identity media retrieval and archival into Supabase Storage
Veriff API auth is HMAC-SHA256 over the session id / media id with X-AUTH-CLIENT + X-HMAC-SIGNATURE
Document-front/back/face images are copied to the customer-documents bucket under veriff/{sessionId}/ and their public URLs written back
Pay-As-You-Go rental finalization: post final pro-rated partial day, then close the rental
Partial-day charge = (dailyRate/24) x hours since last accrual boundary, plus tenant tax and pro-rated service fee
R5: a paused PAYG rental skips the partial-day charge — the admin paused intentionally, so billing dormant time is hostile
Tenant ownership re-validated in-function because service_role bypasses RLS
Accrual day index claimed via unique constraint; a 23505 from the concurrent PAYG cron triggers one re-fetch-and-retry so the partial day is not lost
Vehicle flipped back to Available on close — safe because the DB rental-overlap trigger allows at most one non-terminal rental per vehicle; non-fatal if it fails
Cached AI expense summary per tenant and scope (overall / business / vehicle)
Deliberately imports nothing from ../_shared so it deploys cleanly via the Supabase Management API (MCP)
Highlight chips are computed in code, not by the model, so the numbers can never be hallucinated
Inline OpenAI cost/usage logging via raw PostgREST POST to openai_usage_logs
Multi-report CSV/XLSX export engine (payments, P&L, rentals, statements, fines, aging)
Client-supplied tenantId is never trusted — a service_role export would otherwise leak data across tenants; only super admins may override
Export reads six purpose-built reporting views rather than base tables
PDF export path is a 501 stub — only CSV and XLSX are real
Nightly customer-insurance-policy reminder sweep (monthly check + 30/14/7/0-day expiry milestones)
reminder_events.unique_key + ignoring 23505 makes each milestone fire exactly once, so repeat cron runs never spam
One gated, branded operator email per tenant per run instead of per-policy mail; each send isolated so email failure never breaks reminder generation
Policy state transition Active -> Expired; the source query only pulls Active rows so the lapse bell fires once
AI summary of internal staff reviews for one customer, upserted into customer_review_summaries
Server-side subscription paywall: the hard block was browser-only, so a grace-expired tenant could keep spending OpenAI credit with a saved JWT
Public per-tenant Apply/lead form shape (hidden steps, required overrides, welcome message)
tenants.lead_management_enabled === false hard-disables the public apply endpoint with a 403
Fetch a signed rental agreement — stored PDF first, else download from BoldSign as base64
A previously stored signed document short-circuits the BoldSign call and is served from the customer-documents bucket
BoldSign test/live key resolved from rentals.boldsign_mode with a tenant-level fallback
The BoldSign envelope id is still stored in the legacy rentals.docusign_envelope_id column
PDF is base64-encoded in 0x8000-byte chunks to avoid a String.fromCharCode stack overflow
Resolve whether the booking flow takes payment automatically or manually
Fallback chain tenant_settings.payment_mode -> org_settings.payment_mode -> org_settings.booking_payment_mode
Vocabulary bridge: portal stores 'automated'|'manual', the booking flow expects 'auto'|'manual'; unknown values default to manual as the safer choice
Generate a fresh Stripe Connect account-onboarding link for a tenant
Connect onboarding always uses the live secret key and refuses to run (503) if it is missing or not sk_live_
Consolidated customer statement of account across every rental in a tenant
This function IS the access boundary: RLS is off on ledger_entries and view_customer_statements is a security-definer view granted to anon, so a raw client filter would not be one
Dual-mode caller resolution: a customer_users row yields only that customer's own statement; an app_user of the tenant may request any customer that belongs to the tenant
paid is derived as charged - outstanding rather than summing Payment rows, because a raw Payment row can predate FIFO application and would double-count
Vehicle registration is nulled on the statement when the tenant's plate-privacy flag is on (serves both customer PDFs and staff views)
DB/schema error text is logged server-side but never returned, because this is a financial endpoint
Serve the tenant-appropriate Stripe publishable key and mode to the browser
Return the tenant's platform subscription row plus live Stripe subscription (expanded payment method + latest invoice)
Stripe account chosen from tenant_subscriptions.stripe_account ('uk' for rows predating the UAE migration), falling back to the tenant's configured subscription account
A Stripe read failure is logged and swallowed so the DB-backed subscription still renders
Admin booking-notification email for chauffeur / close-protection bookings (Drive 917)
Anomaly: name says nothing about its job, and branding, phone number and address are hardcoded to one tenant with no tenants lookup or per-tenant template
Cancel INSHUR/ABI Period Z cover that has not started yet
ABI only allows Cancel before the period begins, so a started period silently falls back to End — and the response says which happened, because the two are not the same thing to an operator
hasStarted() renders 'now' into the stored timezone in the same ABI wall-clock format so the comparison is plain string ordering with no offset arithmetic
Get Rentals probe after a failure — a failed Cancel and an already-cancelled period are indistinguishable from ABI's bare {} response
409 when coverage source_mode differs from current INSHUR mode — closing the record while the real policy keeps billing at ABI is the failure being prevented
Deliberately NOT gated on getInshurUsability: cover already bought must always be stoppable, even after a tenant switches INSHUR off
Cancel failure raises an operator bell plus a daily-deduped reminders row; alerting is fully wrapped so it can never fail or mask the operation
Cache-through INSHUR/ABI Period Z vehicle eligibility check (batchable up to 200 vehicles)
Fails CLOSED, unlike bonzah-check-vehicle-eligibility which fails open: a false negative there loses an upsell, a false positive here puts an uninsured rental on the road
12h TTL cache in inshur_vehicle_eligibility, invalidated when source_mode or VIN changes — a simulated pass must never stand in for a real one
Circuit breaker after 3 consecutive transport failures plus a 60s network deadline; remaining vehicles are returned as not_checked instead of hammering a down ABI
A verdict that could not be obtained is never written to the cache, so a thirty-second ABI outage cannot leave a whole fleet marked red
Vehicle ids are regex-prefiltered because Postgres raises invalid-uuid-syntax, which would fail the whole batch for one bad entry
Start INSHUR/ABI Period Z cover for one rental: eligibility -> renter -> rental period -> ID card -> coverage row

ABI has no idempotency key, so the coverage row is claimed as 'pending' BEFORE the billable call; partial unique index idx_inshur_cov_one_active turns a double-fire into a 23505 'already covered' instead of a second policy
An ambiguous create (timeout/network/5xx) leaves the row 'pending' and returns 202 — holding the unique index is the only thing preventing a second non-cancellable policy on the same VIN

Declares its own pickup/return time defaults (00:00:00 / 23:59:00) because four other places in the repo default them differently; widens in the safe direction since under-insuring puts an uninsured driver on the road
start/end are string-concatenated from the date and time columns; routing them through a Date would reinterpret tenant wall-clock in the isolate's UTC zone and shift every rental boundary
Garaging state resolved from vehicles.garaging_state, else scraped from pickup/delivery/tenant address text — mirrors the resolver in bonzah-create-quote
SHA-256 fingerprint of the Add Renter payload: ABI has no update endpoint, so a changed hash is the only signal to re-register a customer whose details were corrected
ID card fetch/upload is best-effort — cover is already active, so a failure is a warning on a success response, never a rollback; the private-bucket PATH is stored, not a URL
Mode appears in both the storage path and the filename so a simulated ID card is unmistakable in a bucket listing or download folder long after it leaves the function
PostgREST 42703 on the vehicles.garaging_state embed is translated to INSHUR_SCHEMA_INCOMPLETE/503 so operators are not sent hunting through their own data for our unapplied migration
Failures are persisted as status='failed'/'ineligible' rows with a real error code, reusing one row per rental so attempt_count reads as attempts and the list shows one line per uninsured rental
End INSHUR/ABI Period Z cover on a rental that has already started
ABI keys End on the VIN and answers failure with a bare {}, so 'already ended' and 'genuinely failed' are disambiguated by a Get Rentals probe before anything is written
End is servicing, not selling, so it skips the usability gate — a tenant who just switched INSHUR off still has live policies accruing on their ABI invoice
409 on mode mismatch: ending a real policy while in simulated mode would mark it ended locally while it keeps billing at ABI
inshur_rental_coverage.rental_id is ON DELETE SET NULL, so a coverage can outlive its rental — and that orphan is exactly the row an operator most needs to stop, because it is still billing
Shared tenant-membership authorization — a valid JWT is not authorisation to act on a tenant, because service_role bypasses RLS
Shared operator in-app notification bell with a dedupeKey (one bell per subject per cause per day)
Shared INSHUR/ABI Period Z API client (config, mode, renter, rental period, eligibility, ID card, Get Rentals)
Shared server-side subscription paywall for billable staff-initiated endpoints
